questions.question: What case does the Khabar of Inna take?
options: Majrur
Marfu'
Mansoob, the same as the Khabar of Kana
Mansoob
questions.explanation: The Khabar of Inna is always Marfu'. While Kana makes the Khabar Mansoob, Inna keeps the Khabar Marfu' and instead makes the Ism (Mubtada) Mansoob.

questions.question: Which type of noun may لا Mushabbeha to Laisa take as its Ism?
options: Nakira (indefinite) only
Ma'rifa (definite) only
Only a pronoun
Both Nakira and Ma'rifa
questions.explanation: لا Mushabbeha comes only with Nakira (indefinite) nouns, unlike ما Mushabbeha which may come with both Ma'rifa and Nakira.

questions.question: When a Siga Sifat after ما نافية shows مُطَابَقَة (agreement in number and gender) with the following noun, what grammatical role does the Sifat play?
options: Mansoob as a Maf'ul Bihi of a hidden verb
The special Mubtada doing Amal on the noun
Khabar Muqaddam — the Ism Zahir is Mubtada Mu'akhkhar
Amil governing the following noun as a Khabar
questions.explanation: If the Sifat matches (مُطَابَقَة) the following noun in number and gender, it is not doing Amal and is therefore Khabar Muqaddam, with the Ism Zahir functioning as Mubtada Mu'akhkhar.

questions.question: What single condition must be met for it to be permissible to place the Maf'ul Bihi before the Fa'il?
options: The verb must be intransitive
Both nouns must carry clear i'rab markings so there is no ambiguity about their roles
The Fa'il must be Ma'rifa (definite)
The Maf'ul must be a pronoun attached to the verb
questions.explanation: Inversion is only permissible when both nouns carry clear i'rab markings, so there is no ambiguity about which is the Fa'il and which is the Maf'ul.

questions.question: Why are أَفْعَالٌ نَاقِصَةٌ called 'incomplete verbs'?
options: They only appear in classical Arabic and are never used in speech
They lack a past tense form in classical Arabic
They cannot take a Maf'ul Bihi in any construction
They cannot form a full sentence with a subject alone; they require both an Ism and a Khabar
questions.explanation: They are incomplete because they cannot form a full sentence with a subject alone; they require both an Ism and a Khabar (a complement structure) to complete their meaning.

questions.question: In the context of the special Mubtada rule, if a Siga Sifat shows مُطَابَقَةٌ with the following noun, what does this reveal about the Sifat's grammatical role?
options: It is a Badal (substitute) for the following noun
It is Mansoob as a Hal (circumstantial clause)
It is the special Mubtada doing Amal on the noun
It is Khabar Muqaddam — mُطَابَقَةٌ shows it is not doing Amal
questions.explanation: Agreement (مُطَابَقَةٌ) means the Sifat is not doing Amal; it is therefore Khabar Muqaddam, with the Ism Zahir functioning as Mubtada Mu'akhkhar.

questions.question: Why can the dropped verb in a سَمَاعِي construction not be re-inserted?
options: These constructions were transmitted from Arab usage as fixed forms — the verb's absence is itself part of the convention
The verb can always be re-inserted; dropping it is merely optional
Re-inserting the verb changes the i'rab of the masdar that follows
The original verb no longer exists in modern Arabic
questions.explanation: Sami constructions were transmitted from Arab usage as fixed forms. The verb's absence is itself part of the established convention and cannot be undone.

questions.question: Which attribute of the cow in Ayah 71 required it to be completely uniform in color?
options: لَا تُثِيرُ الأَرْضَ
لَا ذَلُولٌ
لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا
وَلَا تَسْقِي الحَرْثَ
questions.explanation: لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا means 'no markings of a different color' — requiring a completely uniform yellow cow with no patches or spots of any other color anywhere on its body.

questions.question: According to Ayat 72–73, what was struck against the murdered man's body to miraculously revive him?
options: A piece of the slaughtered cow
A staff carried by Musa عليه السلام
Water from a blessed spring in the valley
Soil from the location of the murder
questions.explanation: Allah commanded them to strike the dead body with a piece of the slaughtered cow. When they did, the man was temporarily revived and named his killer, resolving the murder case miraculously.

questions.question: What grammatical function does the بـ serve in وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ?
options: It indicates instrumentality, meaning 'by means of awareness'
It is an inseparable prefix of غَافِلٍ with no standalone grammatical function
It makes the noun Majrur to indicate a relationship between Allah and the action
زَائِدَة (emphatic) — added after negation to intensify the denial
questions.explanation: The بـ is زَائِدَة (extra/emphatic), added after negation to intensify the denial: Allah is absolutely, completely not unaware.

questions.question: Why did the non-munafiq Jews warn against sharing information about the Prophet ﷺ with Muslims?
options: They feared they would be required to pay Jizyah if they acknowledged the Prophet
They feared Muslims would use it as evidence against them on the Day of Judgment
They wanted to preserve their religious texts as traditions reserved for scholars
They believed the information was too advanced for the early Muslim community to understand
questions.explanation: If they acknowledged the Torah confirms Muhammad ﷺ, on the Day of Judgment Muslims would use that acknowledgment as evidence — 'You knew he was the true Prophet, yet you did not follow him' — strengthening the case against themselves.

questions.question: What does لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا mean, and what does it require of the cow?
options: The cow must never have been sold, traded, or used as collateral
The cow must be young, under two years of age, and unbred
No markings of a different color — the cow must be completely uniform with no patches or spots
The cow must have no physical defects or blemishes of any kind
questions.explanation: لَا شِيَةَ فِيهَا means the cow must be completely uniform in color — not a single patch, spot, or marking of any other color anywhere on its body.

questions.question: What does the Form VI pattern in فَادَّارَأْتُمْ add to the root meaning of دَرَأَ (to push/repel)?
options: Collective agreement — all groups reaching a shared conclusion together
Passive acceptance — the blame being received and absorbed equally by all
Intensive one-directional blame — one group forcefully accusing another
Mutual deflection — each group pushing the accusation toward others
questions.explanation: Form VI adds mutual action between parties. The root دَرَأَ means to push/repel, so فَادَّارَأْتُمْ means each group pushing the blame away from itself toward others — mutual deflection of accusation.

questions.question: How does the phrase عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ intensify the guilt of the Jewish scholars who distorted the Torah?
options: It indicates they had memorized the entire Torah before deciding to distort it
It establishes the distortion was deliberate — they knew the truth and distorted it knowingly, with no plea of ignorance
It shows they acted openly in public without any concealment or shame
It proves they acted under explicit orders from a foreign political authority
questions.explanation: عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ means 'with full insight/awareness.' The scholars heard, understood, and then distorted it knowingly. There is no plea of ignorance or error.

questions.question: Why cannot Witr be elevated to Fard status in the Hanafi madhab?
options: There is no Dalil Qat'i — no Quranic ayah — that could establish a sixth obligatory prayer
The Prophet ﷺ explicitly stated that Witr is a Sunnah and not an obligation
The Miraj established only four obligatory prayers, and Witr fills the fifth slot
The ahadith about Witr are considered too weak to establish any form of obligation
questions.explanation: Witr cannot be Fard because there is no Dalil Qat'i — no Quranic ayah. The Miraj established exactly five obligatory prayers; calling Witr Fard would create a sixth fard that is textually unsupported.

questions.question: According to the Hanafi position, when is Dua al-Qunut recited, and at what point within the rakah?
options: In the third rakah of Witr, before Ruku, throughout the entire year
In every rakah of Witr during Ramadan, recited after completing the surah
Only in the third rakah of Fajr, before Ruku, throughout the entire year
Only during Ramadan, in the third rakah of Witr, after Ruku
questions.explanation: The Hanafi position is that Qunut is recited in the third rakah of Witr, before Ruku, throughout the entire year — not restricted to Ramadan or any particular season.

questions.question: What are the two intentions a Muqtadi must make before the prayer for it to count as Jama'ah?
options: Niyyat al-Mutaba'ah and Niyyat al-Wudu (intention confirming one's state of purity)
Niyyat al-Salah and Niyyat al-Qibla (intention to face the correct direction)
Niyyat al-Fard (obligatory intention) and Niyyat al-Jama'ah (congregation intention)
Niyyat al-Salah (intention for the specific salah) and Niyyat al-Mutaba'ah (intention to follow this Imam)
questions.explanation: The two intentions are Niyyat al-Salah — intention for the specific salah being performed — and Niyyat al-Mutaba'ah — intention to follow this particular Imam. Without both, the prayer does not count as Jama'ah.

questions.question: According to the Ahnaf, what must the congregation do if they discover after Salah that the Imam had no Wudu?
options: The entire congregation must repeat the prayer
The prayer is considered valid for all parties and no repetition is required
Only the Imam must repeat the prayer; the congregation's prayer stands valid
The congregation performs Sajdat al-Sahw and the prayer is accepted
questions.explanation: The Imam being Zamin means his prayer validity carries the congregation. If discovered after Salah that the Imam had no Wudu, the entire congregation must repeat the prayer (Ahnaf position).

questions.question: What type of proof (dalil) distinguishes فَرْض from وَاجِب?
options: Both require Dalil Qat'i but drawn from different categories of Quranic evidence
Fard requires Dalil Qat'i (definitive proof — Quran or mutawatir hadith); Wajib requires Dalil Zanni (probable proof — an emphatic ahad hadith)
Fard requires an ahad hadith; Wajib requires a Quranic ayah
Fard is established by ijma'; Wajib is established by analogical qiyas
questions.explanation: Fard is established by Dalil Qat'i (definitive proof — Quran or mutawatir hadith), while Wajib is established by Dalil Zanni (probable proof — an ahad hadith with taqeed/emphasis). Denying a Fard is kufr; denying a Wajib is not.

questions.question: Leading prayer as a فَاسِق is Makruh Tanzih — what does this mean for the validity of the congregation's Salah?
options: The prayer carries only half the reward of a regular Jama'ah but is not repeated
The prayer is invalid and the congregation must repeat it with a qualified Imam
The prayer is disliked but remains valid; no sin is incurred by the congregation and no repeat is required
The prayer is valid but each Muqtadi individually incurs a sin for participating
questions.explanation: Makruh Tanzih means the prayer is disliked but remains valid. No sin is incurred by the congregation and no repeat is required — avoidance is simply preferred.

questions.question: Which Salahs is recitation from طِوَالُ الْمُفَصَّل Masnoon for, and what is its range?
options: Fajr and Zuhr; Surah al-Hujurat (49) to Surah al-Buruj (85)
Fajr and Asr; Surah al-Baqarah (2) to Surah al-Hujurat (49)
Maghrib and Isha; Surah al-Hujurat (49) to Surah al-Buruj (85)
Zuhr and Asr; Surah al-Buruj (85) to Surah al-Nas (114)
questions.explanation: طِوَالُ الْمُفَصَّل is Masnoon for Fajr and Zuhr. Its range is Surah al-Hujurat (Surah 49) to Surah al-Buruj (Surah 85).
